notes: Brazil was an independent republic (1889), not a Portuguese possession.
Filled colonial Africa from the 1914 map (Libya Ottoman, Congo Free State under Leopold II).
By 1900 almost all of Africa had been claimed by European powers; colonial borders taken from the 1914 map.
North-east New Guinea was German; Papua was British (administered by Australia from 1906).
Filled gaps in the source map from the nearest map (within 50 years).
Filled unclaimed land with peoples and cultures from neighbouring maps.
Named the remaining unclaimed regions after their regional peoples.
Corrected (AP review): Cuba and Puerto Rico were no longer Spanish (1898); Taiwan was Japanese (1895); Hawaii was a US territory (1898); Malaya was under British control.
Territories filed under the wrong realm are moved to their own (for example the islands of South-East Asia, Travancore and Cochin, Cochin China, Sardinia).
Names are the ones in use on this map’s date.

Aegean islands that were in no realm are given to the state that held them: Crete and the islands taken in 1912 to Greece, Rhodes and the Dodecanese to Italy, the rest to the Ottoman Empire before 1912.
The Tukular Caliphate was conquered by France in 1890–1893.
